explanation: In Brazilian social gatherings, hugging is a normal and often expected greeting, even between people who are not especially close. Etiquette sources distinguish a full warm hug from a lighter half-hug or handshake-plus-shoulder-tap, which suits formal or business settings. Refusing all physical warmth can read as distant or arrogant by local standards.
local_tip: At a social gathering, greet each person individually with at least a half-hug or handshake and brief small talk rather than rushing past anyone.
regional_note: Sources note a generational and setting-based variation: full hugs are typical in informal social contexts, while handshakes and half-hugs are preferred in formal or business environments.

also_check.note: Handshakes dominate first meetings; hugs are common among friends but can feel intrusive in professional or new-acquaintance settings.
Bowing is the standard greeting; unsolicited hugging is unusual and can make people uncomfortable, especially in formal contexts.
Handshakes are the norm even among acquaintances; hugs are reserved for close friends and family and may feel overly familiar otherwise.
